the active site of the multicatalytic proteinases has a broad pH activity profile, is not typical of a metallo-, aspa r tic, serine or thiol enzyme, and contains a reactive thiol group that is not a cysteine residue.

multicatalytic protease is an unusual serine proteinase that requires thiol groups for activity, is inhibited by chymostatin but not leupeptin and that it has a broad pH activity profile with activities at acidic, neutral and basic pH.

human multicatalytic (proteasome) proteinase is a thiol-dependent enzyme with an active site that has similarities to serine proteinases but which does not fit the characteristics of any of the four classes of proteinase.

the characterization of the active site and mechanism of action of the multicatalytic proteinases, which may be involved in the regulation of protein degradation in the cytosol.
the identification of the active site and the determination of the mechanism of action of multicatalytic protease.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

multicatalytic protease has an unusual catalytic mechanism that does not involve a metal ion, an aspartic acid, a serine residue or a cysteine residue, but does involve a free thiol and a nucleophilic group that reacts irreversibly with peptidyl halomethanes and aldehydes.
multicatalytic protease is not a metallo-, asparatic, cysteine or serine proteinase, and is inhibited by chymostatin in an unusual manner.
multicatalytic protease does not have the characteristics of any of the known classes of proteinases and that the active site of multicatalytic proteases may be unique.
